# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Trobur Dental Distribution, LLC: review of Furux distribution documents ahead of the Pellmont closing

---

## 1. Bottom Line

The urgent problem is the Pellmont sale. It is a Change of Control under the Distribution Agreement and needs Furux's prior written consent. Nothing in the folder gives that consent, and Amendment No. 1 expressly says it is not consent. If Trobur closes without it, Furux can terminate Trobur's exclusive distributorship.

Five other issues weaken Trobur's position. Two concern risk allocation:
- Furux's product-liability indemnity has been brought under the liability cap.
- The Quality Agreement's narrow "Recall" definition shifts most recall costs to Trobur.

Three concern structure:
- Quality and recall disputes are split off to New Jersey law and a New Jersey forum.
- Furux can assign the agreement to anyone.
- An automatic five-year renewal carries escalating purchase minimums.

The consent request is our best leverage to fix the rest. We should ask for consent and a corrective Amendment No. 2 at the same time.

### Priority Summary

| # | Priority | Issue | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **High: before closing** | Pending Sale needs Furux consent, which has not been given | DA §14.2; Amend. No. 1 Recital B and §5.2 | Get Furux's written consent; make it a UPA closing condition |
| 2 | **High** | Furux product-liability indemnity now capped | DA §§11.2, 11.3; Amend. No. 1 §3.1 | Amend §11.3 to carve out §9.6 |
| 3 | **High** | Narrow QA "Recall" definition cuts back Furux's recall-cost duty | QA §1.1, §1.2; DA §§2.3, 7.4 | Conform QA definition to DA's broad one |
| 4 | **Medium** | NJ law and Mercer County forum govern quality and recall disputes | QA §12; DA §2.3 | Conform QA to Delaware, or carve law and forum out of §2.3 |
| 5 | **Medium** | Furux may assign freely, including to a competitor | DA §14.1 | Add consent standard, limits and a termination right |
| 6 | **Medium (calendar now)** | Five-year auto-renewal; 30-day window; 8% escalating minimums | DA §§1.1, 3.2, 3.3, 5.2 | Calendar Sept. 2 to Oct. 1, 2027; renegotiate |

**Abbreviations:** "DA" is the Exclusive Distribution Agreement dated March 1, 2024. "QA" is the Quality Agreement of the same date. "Amendment" is Amendment No. 1 dated September 15, 2026.

---

## 2. Key Background: the Order-of-Precedence Clause (DA §2.3)

Issues 3 and 4 depend on DA §2.3. Under it, if the DA and the QA conflict, **"with respect to Quality Matters, the Quality Agreement shall govern,"** and the DA governs everything else.

"Quality Matters" (DA §1.1) expressly includes "Recalls," complaint handling, product quality and regulatory compliance. QA §1.2 adds that the QA's definitions "apply to all Quality Matters between the Parties."

The Amendment did not change the QA, other than updating cross-references (Amendment §§1.2, 5.3).

---

## 3. Issues in Priority Order

### Issue 1 (HIGH, before closing): Pending Sale is an unconsented Change of Control

**Where:**
- DA §1.1 (definition of "Change of Control") and §14.2
- Amendment Recital B and §5.2

**What the documents say:**
- Recital B records that Trobur Holdings signed a Unit Purchase Agreement on August 3, 2026 to sell **all** of Trobur's units to Pellmont Dental Group, LLC. As of September 15, 2026 the sale had not closed.
- A transfer of more than 50% of Trobur's equity is a Change of Control under clause (a) of the definition.
- DA §14.2 deems any Change of Control an assignment requiring **Furux's prior written consent**.
- If a Change of Control happens without consent, Furux may terminate on 30 days' notice. It must give that notice within 120 days after it learns of the Change of Control.

**Why consent has not been obtained:**
- Furux signed the Amendment knowing about the sale, but that signature is **not** consent.
- Amendment §5.2 says the Amendment, "including its Recitals, does not constitute a consent or waiver under any provision of the Agreement."
- DA §16.5 also requires any waiver to be in writing and signed by the waiving party.
- No consent appears anywhere in the folder.

**Why it matters:**
- Closing without consent would leave Trobur's core asset, exclusive distribution in an expanded territory, terminable at Furux's option.
- That would likely breach Holdings' representations to Pellmont and affect deal value.
- A purported assignment in breach of §14 is also "void" (DA §14.3). This adds argument risk, although the express remedy is termination.
- Knowing it holds this right, Furux has leverage. It may use the consent request to extract concessions, such as higher minimums or broader Exhibit C carve-outs.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Send Furux a formal written consent request now. Use DA §16.4 notice mechanics and Furux's new notice address under Amendment §4.1.
2. The consent should be unconditional and specific to the Pending Sale. It should confirm that:
   - the DA, the QA and the exclusivity under §2.1 continue unaffected;
   - Furux waives its §14.2 termination right for this transaction.
3. Make Furux's consent an express closing condition in the UPA, or confirm it already is. Do not close without it.
4. Package the consent request with the corrective Amendment No. 2 described in Issues 2 to 6. That way Trobur's concessions, if any, buy those fixes.

### Issue 2 (HIGH): Furux's product-liability indemnity is now subject to the liability cap

**Where:**
- DA §11.2 (the cap) and §11.3(a) (the carve-out)
- Amendment §3.1 (new §9.6) and §3.2 (revised §10.1)

**What the documents say:**
- DA §11.2 caps each party's aggregate liability at the amounts Trobur paid Furux in the 12 months before the claim.
- DA §11.3(a) excludes from the cap "a party's indemnification obligations **under Section 10**."
- As originally signed, §10.1(b) contained Furux's indemnity against Product Claims, including patient-injury claims, so that indemnity was uncapped.
- Amendment §3.1 deletes §10.1(b) and "restate[s]" it as new **§9.6**. Section 11.3 was not touched.

**Result:**
- Furux's Product Claims indemnity now sits outside the carve-out.
- It is limited to roughly one year of purchases. Under the §5.2 minimums for the current Contract Year, that is about $2.8M.
- The §11.1 exclusion of consequential and similar damages may also now apply to it.
- Meanwhile, Trobur's own indemnities to Furux under §10.2 remain in Section 10 and stay **uncapped**.

**Why it matters:**
- Trobur resells scanners, milling units and zirconia blocks used to make restorations for patients.
- Patient-injury claims are its largest third-party exposure. As reseller, Trobur will be named in them.
- A serious injury, or a defect affecting a lot of zirconia blocks, could easily exceed the cap and leave Trobur funding the excess.
- The change was presented as a reorganization, so the client may not appreciate that it gave something up.
- An argument that the parties intended no substantive change is available, but it is uncertain. We should not rely on it.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend §11.3(a) to read "a Party's indemnification obligations under Section 9.6 or Section 10."
- Better still, use "any Party's defense and indemnification obligations under this Agreement, wherever located."
- Alternatively, move §9.6 back into Section 10.
- Ask Furux to confirm in writing that no substantive change was intended.
- In the meantime, confirm that Furux carries products-liability coverage naming Trobur as an additional insured, as DA §16.1 requires (see Open Items).

### Issue 3 (HIGH): The QA's narrow "Recall" definition cuts back Furux's recall-cost obligation

**Where:**
- QA §1.1 (definition of "Recall") and §1.2
- DA §1.1 (definition of "Recall"), §2.3 and §7.4

**The two definitions:**
- **DA definition (broad):** "Recall" covers any recall, market withdrawal, removal, field correction, field safety notice or similar action, "whether voluntary or mandated."
- **QA definition (narrow):** "Recall" is only a removal or correction "**mandated by order of the FDA** or another Governmental Authority," for example a mandatory recall under 21 C.F.R. Part 810.

**How they interact:**
- DA §7.4 requires Furux to bear "**all costs of any Recall**." This includes Trobur's costs of notifying Customers and of retrieving, replacing and crediting products at clinics.
- Recalls are a Quality Matter. Under DA §2.3 and QA §1.2, the QA definition controls where the two conflict.

**Result:**
- Furux's cost obligation reaches only government-ordered recalls.
- Voluntary recalls, market withdrawals and field corrections fall outside it, and Trobur bears those costs. These include Furux-initiated actions under 21 C.F.R. Part 806, which are by far the most common field actions for dental devices.
- Under DA §7.4, Furux alone decides whether to start a Recall. Furux could therefore control both whether a voluntary field action happens and, in effect, who pays for it.
- The QA's operational recall procedures in Section 8 are also tied to the narrow definition. Voluntary actions have no agreed process.

**Why it matters:**
- Trobur performs recall execution in the field (QA §8.3; QA Exhibit 2).
- Retrieval, replacement and crediting across a large installed base of scanners and milling units is expensive, and Trobur would absorb it.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend QA §1.1 so that "Recall" has the meaning given in the DA, covering both voluntary and mandated actions.
- Alternatively, amend DA §7.4 to say that its cost allocation applies to any Recall as defined in the DA, notwithstanding DA §2.3 or any QA definition.
- Extend QA §8 procedures to voluntary actions.

### Issue 4 (MEDIUM): New Jersey law and Mercer County forum govern quality and recall disputes

**Where:**
- QA §12.1 and §12.2
- DA §2.3, §15.1 and §15.2

**What the documents say:**
- **DA:** Delaware law (§15.1) and exclusive New Castle County, Delaware courts (§15.2).
- **QA §12:** the QA "and all disputes concerning Quality Matters" are governed by **New Jersey** law. Actions must be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts of **Mercer County, New Jersey**, which is Furux's home county.
- Standing alone, a forum clause in an ancillary agreement might yield to the main contract. Here, though, DA §2.3 gives the QA precedence on Quality Matters, so the New Jersey choice controls quality and recall disputes.

**Result:**
- Recall cost disputes, product quality disputes and related warranty and complaint disputes go to New Jersey under New Jersey law.
- All other disputes go to Delaware under Delaware law.
- A single dispute, for example a recall-cost claim under DA §7.4 joined with a breach-of-warranty or indemnity claim, could be split across two courts. That raises the risk of inconsistent results and duplicated cost.
- The DA's §15.3 escalation step and §15.4 jury waiver may not reach the New Jersey proceedings.

**Why it matters:** Trobur's most valuable claims against Furux are likely to be quality and recall claims. Those would have to be brought in Furux's home forum, under a law different from the rest of the deal.

**Recommended fix:** Choose one of the following.
- Amend QA §12 to adopt DA §§15.1 to 15.4, so Delaware law, the New Castle County forum, escalation and jury waiver apply.
- Amend DA §2.3 to provide that governing law, forum and dispute-resolution provisions are not Quality Matters and are governed solely by the DA.

### Issue 5 (MEDIUM): Furux may assign the DA to anyone, including a Trobur competitor

**Where:** DA §14.1. QA §13.4 and Guaranty §8.5 follow any permitted assignment.

**What the documents say:**
- Furux may assign the DA, or any of its rights or obligations, "in whole or in part, **to any Person without the consent of Distributor**."
- Furux need only give notice within 30 days **after** the assignment.
- Trobur, by contrast, cannot assign at all without consent (§14.2).

**Why it matters:**
- Furux could assign to a competing dental distributor, a rival manufacturer, or a buyer of the product line that has its own channel.
- That assignee would control Trobur's supply during the exclusive term.
- It would also receive Trobur's customer-level sales, resale pricing and installed-base data under DA §6.2.
- Because partial assignment is allowed, supply obligations could be split from warranty or indemnity obligations, potentially stranding Trobur's recourse.
- The Guaranty and QA would travel with the assignment.
- Trobur would have no consent right and no exit.

**Recommended fix:**
- Require Trobur's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
- Permit assignment without consent only to a successor to all or substantially all of the Furux product-line business that:
  - assumes all obligations in writing; and
  - is not a Trobur competitor or a clinic operator competing with Trobur's customers.
- Prohibit partial assignment.
- Require advance notice.
- Give Trobur a termination right on an assignment to a competitor, with inventory repurchase on the DA §13.3(b) terms.
- Bar the assignee from using DA §6.2 data except as §6.3 permits.

### Issue 6 (MEDIUM, calendar now): Five-year auto-renewal with a 30-day window and escalating minimums

**Where:** DA §1.1 (definitions of "Renewal Term" and "Non-Renewal Window"), §3.2, §3.3, §5.2 and §5.3.

**What the documents say:**
- At the end of the Initial Term (February 29, 2028), the DA renews automatically for a **five-Contract-Year** Renewal Term, and keeps doing so.
- The only way out is a Non-Renewal Notice delivered during the **30-day** window beginning 180 days before the end of the term. A notice outside the window "has no effect."
- For the Initial Term, the window runs from about **September 2 to October 1, 2027**. We should confirm the day-count convention and give notice comfortably inside the window.
- Under §3.3, each Renewal Term carries forward §5.2.

**The minimums:**
- The Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment started at $2.4M and compounds 8% a year: about $3.02M in Contract Year 4.
- It would continue rising through a renewal: about $3.27M, $3.53M, $3.81M, $4.11M and $4.44M.
- That is roughly **$19.2M** of minimum purchases over the first Renewal Term.

**Why it matters:**
- Missing a narrow window locks Trobur into five more years of rising minimums.
- Shortfalls carry a 15% shortfall charge and possible loss of exclusivity under §5.3.
- Holdings' guaranty continues through Renewal Terms (Guaranty §2.3).
- The obligation binds both parties, but it hurts Trobur more because the minimums run only against Trobur.
- The point is especially relevant now: Pellmont's ownership may change Trobur's strategy, and Pellmont will want to know what it is buying.

**Recommended fix:**
- Docket the window now, with reminders, and confirm ownership of the docket post-closing.
- Renegotiate the renewal mechanics:
  - one- or two-year renewals;
  - a longer notice window, for example notice any time up to 90 days before expiry;
  - minimums reset by mutual agreement for each Renewal Term, or capped at 3 to 4% annual growth.

---

## 4. Documents Reviewed With No Issue Found

**Office and Showroom Lease (Ashgrove, Newark):**
- Lease §9.2(c) expressly permits a transfer of all of Trobur's equity without landlord consent. Notice is due 10 days before the transfer, or within 10 days after it if confidentiality bars advance notice.
- No consent issue for the Pending Sale. The deal team should simply diary the notice.

**Certificate of Insurance (Feb. 24, 2026):**
- This evidences Trobur's own coverage for the landlord. The landlord is the certificate holder.
- The CGL limits ($2M per occurrence; $5M aggregate; $5M products-completed operations) meet DA §16.1 minimums.
- It says nothing about Furux's coverage. See Open Items.

**Parent Guaranty:** I found no defect requiring action under the DA. Note the closing points below.

---

## 5. Open Items We Cannot Resolve From the Folder

1. **UPA terms.** The Unit Purchase Agreement is not in the folder. We need to confirm:
   - the expected closing date;
   - whether Furux consent is a closing condition;
   - the seller's representations about material contracts.
2. **Status of consent.** We need to know whether Trobur or Holdings has already asked Furux for consent, and whether Furux has responded.
3. **Holdings' guaranty after closing.** The guaranty survives a change in Trobur's ownership (Guaranty §4.1(c)). Holdings, as seller, will want to be released.
   - Guaranty §7.2 allows release only for future obligations, and only if Furux accepts a replacement guaranty, presumably from Pellmont.
   - This should be negotiated alongside the consent.
4. **Furux's insurance.** We have no certificate showing Furux's products-liability coverage naming Trobur as additional insured (DA §16.1). Given Issue 2, we should request one.
5. **Purchase volume.** We need Trobur's actual 12-month purchase figures to size the effective cap in Issue 2.
6. **Intent behind Amendment §3.** Negotiation history and drafts may support an argument that moving the indemnity was not meant to change the cap.
7. **Pellmont as Customer or national account.** Pellmont is a multi-state clinic operator. We should check:
   - whether it appears on Furux's Exhibit C national-accounts schedule, which is not in the folder;
   - whether post-closing sales to Pellmont clinics would be diverted to Furux's direct channel.
8. **Past recall practice.** We should ask whether the parties have handled any voluntary field actions to date, and who paid for them. A course of dealing could affect how Issue 3 plays out.

---

## 6. Recommended Next Steps

1. **This week:** Confirm the UPA closing timeline and conditions. Send Furux the consent request (Issue 1).
2. **In parallel:** Prepare a draft Amendment No. 2 covering:
   - the §11.3 carve-out (Issue 2);
   - conforming the Recall definition (Issue 3);
   - governing law and forum (Issue 4);
   - §14.1 assignment limits (Issue 5);
   - renewal and minimums (Issue 6);
   - a guaranty replacement mechanism.
3. **Docket** the September 2 to October 1, 2027 Non-Renewal Window. Send the lease §9.2 notice reminder to the deal team.
4. **Brief the client and Pellmont's counsel** on Issues 1 and 2. They affect deal certainty and value.

# MEMORANDUM

**TO:** Supervising Partner
**FROM:** Associate
**DATE:** November 20, 2026
**RE:** Trobur Dental Distribution, LLC – Review of Furux Distribution Arrangement Ahead of Pending Sale to Pellmont Dental Group

---

## 1. Purpose and Bottom Line

You asked me to review the six documents in the Trobur/Furux folder before the sale of Trobur to Pellmont Dental Group, LLC closes. I reviewed:

- the Exclusive Distribution Agreement dated March 1, 2024 (the "**EDA**");
- Amendment No. 1 dated September 15, 2026 (the "**Amendment**");
- the Parent Guaranty of Trobur Holdings, Inc.;
- the Quality Agreement dated March 1, 2024 (the "**QA**");
- the Newark office and showroom lease;
- the February 2026 certificate of insurance.

**Bottom line:**

- **Most urgent issue.** The Pending Sale is a Change of Control. It requires Furux's prior written consent, and that consent has not been given. If the sale closes without consent, Furux may terminate Trobur's exclusive appointment on 30 days' notice. Consent should be obtained, and made a closing condition, before anything else.
- **Quality Agreement overrides.** Two Quality Agreement provisions displace the EDA on the issues that matter most for a medical device distributor:
  - recall-cost allocation; and
  - governing law and forum for quality disputes.
- **Commercial terms.** Two EDA terms are one-sided against Trobur:
  - Furux may assign the agreement freely; and
  - the agreement renews automatically for five years with a narrow notice window and escalating minimum purchases.

**Recommended approach.** We should use the consent request as leverage to fix as many of these points as possible in a single Amendment No. 2.

**Key structural point.** Section 2.3 of the EDA provides that "with respect to Quality Matters, the Quality Agreement shall govern." The EDA governs all other matters. "Quality Matters" is defined in EDA Section 1.1 and expressly includes Recalls, complaint handling and regulatory compliance. This precedence clause drives Issues 2 and 3 below.

---

## 2. Issues in Priority Order

### Issue 1 – Change of Control: Furux's Consent to the Pending Sale Has Not Been Obtained
**Priority: HIGH / URGENT (pre-closing)**

**Where it appears**
- EDA Section 14.2 and the "Change of Control" definition in Section 1.1.
- Amendment, Recital B and Section 5.2.

**What it says**
- Under Section 14.2, any Change of Control of Trobur is "deemed an assignment of this Agreement requiring the prior written consent of Supplier."
- "Change of Control" includes any acquisition of more than 50% of Trobur's equity.
- Recital B of the Amendment records that Trobur Holdings signed a Unit Purchase Agreement on August 3, 2026. Under it, Holdings will sell **all** of Trobur's outstanding units to Pellmont. The sale had not closed as of September 15, 2026.
- This is plainly a Change of Control.

**The Amendment is not consent**
- Section 5.2 of the Amendment states that the Amendment, "including its Recitals, does not constitute a consent or waiver under any provision of the Agreement."
- Furux therefore signed a document acknowledging the deal while expressly reserving its rights.
- Nothing else in the folder records Furux's consent.

**Why it matters**
- If the sale closes without written consent, Furux may terminate the EDA on 30 days' written notice. It has 120 days after learning of the Change of Control to give that notice (Section 14.2).
- Trobur's main asset is its exclusive appointment for Furux products across an expanded mid-Atlantic territory. Pellmont is presumably paying for that.
- Furux would gain major leverage after closing. It could use the termination threat to reprice the deal or to pull the Additional Territory.

**Recommended fix**
1. Request Furux's prior written consent now, in a stand-alone consent letter that expressly references Section 14.2 and the August 3, 2026 Unit Purchase Agreement.
2. Ask that the consent letter also include:
   - a waiver of the Section 14.2 termination right for this transaction; and
   - confirmation that the EDA, the QA and the Additional Territory continue unaffected after closing.
3. Confirm with deal counsel that Furux consent is a condition to closing under the Unit Purchase Agreement. If it is not, the UPA should be amended (or a closing deliverable added).
4. Use the consent request to negotiate the fixes in Issues 2–5, recognizing that Furux will have the leverage in that negotiation.

---

### Issue 2 – Quality Agreement's Narrow "Recall" Definition Cuts Back Furux's Recall-Cost Obligation
**Priority: HIGH**

**Where it appears**
- QA Section 1.1 (definition of "Recall") and QA Section 1.2.
- EDA Sections 1.1 ("Recall"), 2.3 and 7.4.

**What it says**
- **EDA definition.** The EDA defines "Recall" broadly: "any recall, market withdrawal, removal, field correction, field safety notice or similar field action ... whether voluntary or mandated by any Governmental Authority."
- **EDA cost obligation.** EDA Section 7.4 requires Furux to "bear all costs of any Recall." That includes Trobur's costs of notifying Customers and of retrieving, replacing and crediting product at dental clinics.
- **QA definition.** The QA defines "Recall" as only a removal or correction "mandated by order of the FDA or another Governmental Authority."
- **QA application clause.** QA Section 1.2 provides that the QA definitions "apply to all Quality Matters between the Parties."

**Why it matters**
- Recalls are a Quality Matter. Under EDA Section 2.3, the QA governs in a conflict on Quality Matters, so the narrow definition controls.
- As a result, Furux's cost obligation under Section 7.4 effectively covers only **government-ordered** recalls.
- Most field actions for dental devices are voluntary manufacturer-initiated recalls, market withdrawals, field corrections and safety notices. Typical examples are scanner software and firmware fixes, milling unit corrections and zirconia lot withdrawals. Mandatory FDA recall orders under 21 C.F.R. Part 810 are rare.
- QA Section 8.3 still requires Trobur to stop distribution, notify clinics, and retrieve, replace or correct product at Furux's direction. Trobur would therefore do the work and, on the narrow reading, absorb the cost.
- Furux could also argue that its EDA Section 7.4 right to decide whether to initiate a Recall leaves voluntary actions outside any cost-shifting at all.

**Recommended fix**
- Amend QA Section 1.1 to conform "Recall" to the broad EDA definition (voluntary or mandated, including market withdrawals, field corrections and field safety notices). Alternatively, provide that the EDA definition of "Recall" controls for cost allocation.
- Add an express statement to EDA Section 7.4 that it applies "notwithstanding Section 2.3 or any definition in the Quality Agreement."
- Consider adding a reimbursement mechanic to EDA Section 7.4 covering Trobur's internal labor at the Exhibit D rates and the credit timing.

---

### Issue 3 – Quality Agreement's New Jersey Law and Mercer County Forum Override Delaware for Quality Disputes
**Priority: HIGH**

**Where it appears**
- QA Section 12 (Sections 12.1 and 12.2).
- EDA Sections 2.3, 15.1 and 15.2.

**What it says**
- **EDA.** Sections 15.1 and 15.2 select Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.
- **QA governing law.** QA Section 12.1 provides that the QA "and all disputes concerning Quality Matters are governed by the laws of the State of New Jersey."
- **QA forum.** QA Section 12.2 requires any action "arising out of or relating to this Quality Agreement or any Quality Matter" to be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts of Mercer County, New Jersey.
- **Precedence.** Because EDA Section 2.3 gives the QA precedence on Quality Matters, the New Jersey clause controls disputes about recalls, complaints, nonconforming product and product quality. It does not merely yield to the EDA.

**Why it matters**
- Trobur's most valuable claims against Furux are likely to be quality and recall claims, including recovery of recall costs under Issue 2. Those claims would have to be litigated in Furux's home county (Furux is based in Princeton) under New Jersey law.
- Every other dispute, such as payment, minimums, territory and termination, goes to Delaware under Delaware law.
- A single dispute often has both elements. One example is a recall that leads to a minimum-purchase shortfall or a termination. That creates a real risk of:
  - parallel proceedings in two states;
  - forum fights over characterization; and
  - inconsistent results.
- The EDA Section 15.4 jury waiver and Section 15.3 escalation procedure do not appear in the QA. Quality disputes may therefore proceed without either.

**Recommended fix**

Pick one of the following options.

- **Preferred: conform the QA.** Amend QA Section 12 to adopt Delaware law and the New Castle County forum, and incorporate EDA Sections 15.3 and 15.4.
- **Alternative: carve out the dispute clauses.** Amend EDA Section 2.3 so that the QA's precedence does not extend to governing law, forum, dispute resolution, or allocation of costs and liabilities. Those provisions would always be governed by the EDA.

---

### Issue 4 – Five-Year Automatic Renewal, 30-Day Notice Window and Escalating Minimums
**Priority: MEDIUM-HIGH (calendar now; renegotiate with Issue 1)**

**Where it appears**
- EDA Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3.
- EDA Section 1.1 definitions of "Renewal Term" and "Non-Renewal Window."
- EDA Section 5.2.

**What it says**
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term ends February 29, 2028 (Section 3.1).
- **Automatic renewal.** The EDA "shall renew automatically for successive Renewal Terms" unless a party delivers a Non-Renewal Notice during the Non-Renewal Window. A notice delivered outside the window "has no effect" (Section 3.2).
- **Renewal Term.** A Renewal Term is **five Contract Years**.
- **Notice window.** The Non-Renewal Window is the 30-day period beginning 180 days before the last day of the then-current Term. For the Initial Term, that window runs from approximately **September 2, 2027 to October 1, 2027**.
- **Minimums continue.** Under Section 3.3, renewal terms carry Section 5.2 forward. The Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment started at $2,400,000 and increases 8% per Contract Year, compounded, through any Renewal Term. Excess purchases do not carry forward.

**Why it matters**
- The clause is mutual on its face, but it falls hardest on Trobur. Missing a 30-day window locks Trobur into five more years of rising minimums. My rough figures:

  | Contract Year | Period | Minimum |
  |---|---|---|
  | 5 (first renewal year) | March 2028 | about $3.27 million |
  | 9 | | about $4.44 million |
  | Renewal Term total | | roughly $19.2 million |

- **Shortfall remedies (Section 5.3).** A shortfall triggers a 15% shortfall payment. A shortfall greater than 20% allows Furux to convert Trobur's appointment to non-exclusive.
- **Guaranty exposure.** The Parent Guaranty is continuing through any Renewal Term (Guaranty Sections 2.3 and 4.1(a)), so Holdings' exposure (capped at $3,000,000) also rolls forward.
- **Effect of the sale.** Pellmont's strategy after closing may differ. For example, it may want to self-distribute or consolidate suppliers. The buyer needs to know about this window.

**Recommended fix**
- **Immediate:** docket September 2, 2027 (window opens) and October 1, 2027 (window closes), with internal reminders starting in summer 2027. Confirm the day-count with the client and serve any notice early in the window to avoid an argument over the start date. Make sure the reminder carries over to Pellmont after closing.
- **Renegotiate (ideally in the consent package):**
  - shorten Renewal Terms to one or two years;
  - widen the notice window (for example, any time up to 90 days before expiry);
  - reset or cap minimums at the start of each Renewal Term (for example, mutually agreed minimums, or a cap on escalation in line with the 4% price-increase cap in Section 5.1).

---

### Issue 5 – Furux May Assign the EDA to Anyone, Including a Trobur Competitor, Without Consent
**Priority: MEDIUM**

**Where it appears**
- EDA Section 14.1 (compare Section 14.2).
- See also Guaranty Section 8.5 and QA Section 13.4, which follow any permitted EDA assignment.

**What it says**
- Section 14.1 allows Furux to assign the EDA "or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, to any Person without the consent of Distributor." Its only obligation is notice within 30 days **after** the assignment takes effect.
- Trobur, by contrast, cannot assign without consent, and its own change of control counts as an assignment (Section 14.2).

**Why it matters**
- Nothing prevents Furux from assigning the EDA to:
  - a competing dental distributor;
  - a competitor of Pellmont; or
  - a buyer of only part of the Furux product line. The "in part" wording would allow splitting obligations, for example assigning consumables but keeping scanners.
- The assignee would control supply to Trobur during the exclusive term.
- The assignee would also receive Trobur's competitively sensitive data under EDA Section 6.2 and QA Section 5: clinic-level unit sales, resale prices, installed base by serial number, and customer names and addresses.
- Trobur has no consent right, no termination right and no protection beyond the EDA Section 12 confidentiality covenant. Furux's covenant would transfer to the assignee.

**Recommended fix**
- Revise Section 14.1 to require Trobur's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. The only exception should be an assignment of the entire EDA to a successor to all or substantially all of the Furux business or product line that:
  1. is not a competitor of Trobur (or of its Affiliates, which after closing will include Pellmont);
  2. assumes all obligations in writing; and
  3. takes the QA together with the EDA.
- Prohibit partial assignment.
- Give Trobur a termination right (with the Section 13.3 inventory repurchase) on any assignment to a competitor.
- Restrict the assignee's use of Section 6.2 data.
